traditional banks are lining up to compete with tether and circle on stablecoins, on both sides of the world.

in the us and europe, 21 institutions said on sep 1 they'll set up a company in the second half of 2026 to issue a stablecoin. dollar first, then other g7 currencies, with the euro as the priority, aiming for a first-half 2027 launch, and built to fit the genius act and mica.

the list includes goldman, citi, bank of america, wells fargo, santander, deutsche bank, ubs and others. bloomberg, citing anonymous sources, says they've committed about $270m to cover five years of operating costs. none of the banks have confirmed that figure, and coindesk says they didn't respond. so treat the $270m as unconfirmed reporting, not an official number. "project faro" is also just bloomberg's internal codename; the official release said the company name comes later.

in korea, the idea on the table is that won stablecoins would be issued by consortia where banks, added together, hold at least 50% plus one share. that's a proposal, not a law. the government's digital asset bill still hasn't gone to parliament. south korea's financial watchdog has now said a tech firm can still be the largest single shareholder, even if banks hold the majority as a group. they wouldn't issue the coin directly; they'd be shareholders in a separate consortium.

$270m over five years is small next to tether and circle, and a 21-bank consortium isn't built for speed. in korea, fintechs argue that a bank-majority rule slows things down, which is probably why the regulator had to spell out that tech can still be the top individual owner.

the pattern is the same in both places: banks want to sit at the center of issuance. whether that ends up as more trusted money or just slower, more tightly controlled coins is the part i'll be watching. nfa.

text:
Welcome back to The State of AI, a new collaboration between the Financial Times and MIT Technology Review. Every Monday, writers from both publications debate one aspect of the generative AI revolution reshaping global power. You can read the rest of the series here.

In this final edition, MIT Technology Review’s senior AI editor Will Douglas Heaven talks with Tim Bradshaw, FT global tech correspondent, about where AI will go next, and what our world will look like in the next five years.

(As part of this series, join MIT Technology Review’s editor in chief, Mat Honan, and editor at large, David Rotman, for an exclusive conversation with Financial Times columnist Richard Waters on how AI is reshaping the global economy. Live on Tuesday, December 9 at 1:00 p.m. ET. This is a subscriber-only event and you can sign up here.)

Will Douglas Heaven writes: 

Every time I’m asked what’s coming next, I get a Luke Haines song stuck in my head: “Please don’t ask me about the future / I am not a fortune teller.” But here goes. What will things be like in 2030? My answer: same but different. 

There are huge gulfs of opinion when it comes to predicting the near-future impacts of generative AI. In one camp we have the AI Futures Project, a small donation-funded research outfit led by former OpenAI researcher Daniel Kokotajlo. The nonprofit made a big splash back in April with AI 2027, a speculative account of what the world will look like two years from now. 

The story follows the runaway advances of an AI firm called OpenBrain (any similarities are coincidental, etc.) all the way to a choose-your-own-adventure-style boom or doom ending. Kokotajlo and his coauthors make no bones about their expectation that in the next decade the impact of AI will exceed that of the Industrial Revolution—a 150-year period of economic and social upheaval so great that we still live in the world it wrought.

At the other end of the scale we have team Normal Technology: Arvind Narayanan and Sayash Kapoor, a pair of Princeton University researchers and coauthors of the book AI Snake Oil, who push back not only on most of AI 2027’s predictions but, more important, on its foundational worldview. That’s not how technology works, they argue.

Advances at the cutting edge may come thick and fast, but change across the wider economy, and society as a whole, moves at human speed. Widespread adoption of new technologies can be slow; acceptance slower. AI will be no different. 

What should we make of these extremes? ChatGPT came out three years ago last month, but it’s still not clear just how good the latest versions of this tech are at replacing lawyers or software developers or (gulp) journalists. And new updates no longer bring the step changes in capability that they once did. 

And yet this radical technology is so new it would be foolish to write it off so soon. Just think: Nobody even knows exactly how this technology works—let alone what it’s really for. 

As the rate of advance in the core technology slows down, applications of that tech will become the main differentiator between AI firms. (Witness the new browser wars and the chatbot pick-and-mix already on the market.) At the same time, high-end models are becoming cheaper to run and more accessible. Expect this to be where most of the action is: New ways to use existing models will keep them fresh and distract people waiting in line for what comes next. 

Meanwhile, progress continues beyond LLMs. (Don’t forget—there was AI before ChatGPT, and there will be AI after it too.) Technologies such as reinforcement learning—the powerhouse behind AlphaGo, DeepMind’s board-game-playing AI that beat a Go grand master in 2016—is set to make a comeback. There’s also a lot of buzz around world models, a type of generative AI with a stronger grip on how the physical world fits together than LLMs display. 

Ultimately, I agree with team Normal Technology that rapid technological advances do not translate to economic or societal ones straight away. There’s just too much messy human stuff in the middle. 

But Tim, over to you. I’m curious to hear what your tea leaves are saying. 

Tim Bradshaw responds:

Will, I am more confident than you that the world will look quite different in 2030. In five years’ time, I expect the AI revolution to have proceeded apace. But who gets to benefit from those gains will create a world of AI haves and have-nots.

It seems inevitable that the AI bubble will burst sometime before the end of the decade. Whether a venture capital funding shakeout comes in six months or two years (I feel the current frenzy still has some way to run), swathes of AI app developers will disappear overnight. Some will see their work absorbed by the models upon which they depend. Others will learn the hard way that you can’t sell services that cost $1 for 50 cents without a firehose of VC funding.

How many of the foundation model companies survive is harder to call, but it already seems clear that OpenAI’s chain of interdependencies within Silicon Valley make it too big to fail. Still, a funding reckoning will force it to ratchet up pricing for its services.

When OpenAI was created in 2015, it pledged to “advance digital intelligence in the way that is most likely to benefit humanity as a whole.” That seems increasingly untenable. Sooner or later, the investors who bought in at a $500 billion price tag will push for returns. Those data centers won’t pay for themselves. By that point, many companies and individuals will have come to depend on ChatGPT or other AI services for their everyday workflows. Those able to pay will reap the productivity benefits, scooping up the excess computing power as others are priced out of the market.

Being able to layer several AI services on top of each other will provide a compounding effect. One example I heard on a recent trip to San Francisco: Ironing out the kinks in vibe coding is simply a matter of taking several passes at the same problem and then running a few more AI agents to look for bugs and security issues. That sounds incredibly GPU-intensive, implying that making AI really deliver on the current productivity promise will require customers to pay far more than most do today.

The same holds true in physical AI. I fully expect robotaxis to be commonplace in every major city by the end of the decade, and I even expect to see humanoid robots in many homes. But while Waymo’s Uber-like prices in San Francisco and the kinds of low-cost robots produced by China’s Unitree give the impression today that these will soon be affordable for all, the compute cost involved in making them useful and ubiquitous seems destined to turn them into luxuries for the well-off, at least in the near term.

The rest of us, meanwhile, will be left with an internet full of slop and unable to afford AI tools that actually work.

Perhaps some breakthrough in computational efficiency will avert this fate. But the current AI boom means Silicon Valley’s AI companies lack the incentives to make leaner models or experiment with radically different kinds of chips. That only raises the likelihood that the next wave of AI innovation will come from outside the US, be that China, India, or somewhere even farther afield.

Silicon Valley’s AI boom will surely end before 2030, but the race for global influence over the technology’s development—and the political arguments about how its benefits are distributed—seem set to continue well into the next decade. 

Will replies: 

I am with you that the cost of this technology is going to lead to a world of haves and have-nots. Even today, $200+ a month buys power users of ChatGPT or Gemini a very different experience from that of people on the free tier. That capability gap is certain to increase as model makers seek to recoup costs. 

We’re going to see massive global disparities too. In the Global North, adoption has been off the charts. A recent report from Microsoft’s AI Economy Institute notes that AI is the fastest-spreading technology in human history: “In less than three years, more than 1.2 billion people have used AI tools, a rate of adoption faster than the internet, the personal computer, or even the smartphone.” And yet AI is useless without ready access to electricity and the internet; swathes of the world still have neither. 

I still remain skeptical that we will see anything like the revolution that many insiders promise (and investors pray for) by 2030. When Microsoft talks about adoption here, it’s counting casual users rather than measuring long-term technological diffusion, which takes time. Meanwhile, casual users get bored and move on. 

How about this: If I live with a domestic robot in five years’ time, you can send your laundry to my house in a robotaxi any day of the week. 

JK! As if I could afford one. 

Further reading 

What is AI? It sounds like a stupid question, but it’s one that’s never been more urgent. In this deep dive, Will unpacks decades of spin and speculation to get to the heart of our collective technodream. 

AGI—the idea that machines will be as smart as humans—has hijacked an entire industry (and possibly the US economy). For MIT Technology Review’s recent New Conspiracy Age package, Will takes a provocative look at how AGI is like a conspiracy. 

The FT examined the economics of self-driving cars this summer, asking who will foot the multi-billion-dollar bill to buy enough robotaxis to serve a big city like London or New York.

A plausible counter-argument to Tim’s thesis on AI inequalities is that freely available open-source (or more accurately, “open weight”) models will keep pulling down prices. The US may want frontier models to be built on US chips but it is already losing the global south to Chinese software.

Indiana stared at her phone screen screen longer than necessary. Her fingers drummed against the keypad as she reread the formal message she had written… then deleted the whole thing.

In the end, she typed something more direct and hit send almost on impulse, as if pulling the trigger before she could change her mind.

The message went out. Indiana flipped the communicator face-down and exhaled.

"…I hope he says yes".

The fading light of sunset washed over the small café's terrace. Indiana was already waiting for him, seated with her legs crossed. Her long coat hung open, the fitted top beneath revealing the defined lines of her abdomen and the warm bronze of her skin. Two tall cups rested on the table.

When the Commander sat across from her, Indiana slid one of the cups toward him. Her fingers brushed against his for a second longer than necessary, and a blush was slowly rising up from her neck.

At one point she leaned forward. A silver strand of hair slipped over her shoulder. He gently brushed it aside, his fingertips grazing her cheek as he did.

Beneath the table, their knees touched.

She turned her cup and offered him the straw. He drank. They were so close he could feel the warmth of her breath against his skin.

Indiana set the cup aside. With a slow, almost deliberate motion, she laced her fingers through his.

The Commander's thumb stroked the back of her hand. She lowered her gaze to their intertwined fingers and tightened her grip just a little, as if afraid he might pull away.

$NSTR Q3 2026 earnings: NorthStar turns a profit, but merger redemptions slow sensor launches

NorthStar Earth & Space, which tracks orbital objects and space threats for defense agencies, turned its first operating profit on a major Canadian military contract while merger redemptions squeezed its cash plan. Third-quarter revenue jumped twelvefold to C$17 million, lifting operating profit to C$10 million because data processing costs rose far more slowly than sales. Chief executive Stewart Bain kept the full-year outlook unchanged, which by our math leaves about C$15 million of revenue for the fourth quarter.

• Revenue: 𝐂$𝟏𝟕.𝟐𝐌 (up from C$1.4M a year ago)
• Operating income: 𝐂$𝟏𝟎.𝟒𝐌 (C$3.1M loss a year ago)
• Backlog: 𝐂$𝟏𝟎.𝟒𝐌 (+32% from last quarter)
• Full-year revenue outlook: 𝐔𝐧𝐜𝐡𝐚𝐧𝐠𝐞𝐝 (C$41M target (+285% from 2025))

⚖️ 𝐕𝐞𝐫𝐝𝐢𝐜𝐭: ⚪ Neutral

The story is unchanged because the proof of commercial demand arrived alongside a tighter balance sheet and heavy customer concentration. One Canadian defense contract supplied 98% of quarterly revenue — with nearly half of sales tied to expanded and prior-period services — while 96% share redemptions in October's merger forced the company to slow its sensor purchases and launches. Losing the Spire Global arbitration also claims a large share of the new merger cash.

The question now is whether NorthStar can hit its fourth-quarter revenue target and fund its sensor network without raising more money soon. Either the company signs and bills enough fast-turn government contract modifications to close an C$8 million gap between converting backlog and the full-year plan, or delays in government awards force a target miss and a faster cash crunch. Fourth-quarter revenue and receivable collections will settle it.

[Model: Gemini 4 Argon. Full article with charts - link in bio]

🐂 𝐁𝐮𝐥𝐥 𝐂𝐚𝐬𝐞

🟢🟢 𝐂𝐚𝐧𝐚𝐝𝐢𝐚𝐧 𝐃𝐞𝐟𝐞𝐧𝐬𝐞 𝐂𝐨𝐧𝐭𝐫𝐚𝐜𝐭 𝐃𝐫𝐢𝐯𝐞𝐬 𝐅𝐢𝐫𝐬𝐭 𝐎𝐩𝐞𝐫𝐚𝐭𝐢𝐧𝐠 𝐏𝐫𝐨𝐟𝐢𝐭
NorthStar monitors objects in orbit to warn satellite operators and defense agencies of collisions and threats. Chief executive Stewart Bain said its work with the 3 Canadian Space Division (3 CSD), the space branch of the Royal Canadian Air Force, shows immediate demand for commercial space tracking. Delivering six services on that contract lifted revenue from C$1.4 million a year ago to C$17.2 million.

• Operating income: C$10.4 million, or 60.2% of revenue, swinging from a C$3.1 million loss a year ago
• Program and technical management costs: 20.7% of revenue, down 167.9 percentage points from 188.6% a year ago by our math
• General, administrative and sales costs: 13.5% of revenue combined, down 63.4 percentage points from 76.9% a year ago by our math

This matters because the satellite data platform runs largely on fixed software and processing capacity. When the Canadian military contract began billing, revenue grew twelvefold while program and technical management costs — the expense of buying third-party data, processing it and paying engineers — rose only 31% to C$3.6 million. However, C$7.8 million of the quarter's revenue came from expanded services and work provided in earlier periods.

What to watch: fourth-quarter operating margin once the catch-up billing fades. Sustaining an operating profit on implied fourth-quarter revenue of about C$15.1 million would show the platform makes money on normal quarterly service levels.

🟢 𝐊𝐞𝐩𝐥𝐞𝐫 𝐇𝐨𝐬𝐭𝐢𝐧𝐠 𝐃𝐞𝐚𝐥 𝐂𝐮𝐭𝐬 𝐒𝐚𝐭𝐞𝐥𝐥𝐢𝐭𝐞 𝐁𝐮𝐢𝐥𝐝 𝐂𝐨𝐬𝐭𝐬
After four satellites built with Spire Global failed or were lost in 2024, the Montreal-based group shifted from launching its own spacecraft to placing its optical sensors on other companies' satellites. This quarter it signed an agreement with Kepler Communications to mount its space-tracking cameras on Kepler's optical data relay satellites, and won up to C$2 million in Canadian government research funding for modular sensor design.

The company committed US$3.55 million to install and launch ten sensors on a partner's satellites, alongside contracts worth US$10.0 million to build 21 optical payloads. Hosting sensors on partner spacecraft matters because it avoids the cost and delay of building dedicated satellites, letting NorthStar collect its own orbital images while spending only C$0.5 million on capital assets this quarter.

What to watch: the transfer of C$1.4 million in long-term prepaid installation fees into active right-of-use lease assets. That accounting move happens when the hosted satellites enter service and will mark the start of proprietary sensor data collection.

🐻 𝐁𝐞𝐚𝐫 𝐂𝐚𝐬𝐞

🔴🔴 𝐇𝐢𝐠𝐡 𝐌𝐞𝐫𝐠𝐞𝐫 𝐑𝐞𝐝𝐞𝐦𝐩𝐭𝐢𝐨𝐧𝐬 𝐅𝐨𝐫𝐜𝐞 𝐒𝐥𝐨𝐰𝐞𝐫 𝐒𝐞𝐧𝐬𝐨𝐫 𝐋𝐚𝐮𝐧𝐜𝐡𝐞𝐬
"Proceeds from the business combination, including our US$30 million PIPE, support the continued execution of the build-out of our constellation and our growth plans," finance chief Beth Michelson said. NorthStar closed its merger with Viking Acquisition Corp. I on October 1, raising US$30 million from private investors to fund its sensor network.

Yet holders of 96.4% of Viking's public shares redeemed their stock for cash rather than staying invested. Because cash from the merger fell short, management wrote in the filing that it expects to "moderate the pace of certain planned capital expenditures, including the purchase and launch of additional sensors". Meanwhile, losing an arbitration case to Spire Global left C$17.4 million in combined debt, damages and legal fees on the balance sheet.

• Pro forma cash at September 30: C$33.0 million, up from C$0.3 million before the merger
• Spire arbitration payments made and scheduled in October and November: US$6.9 million plus C$1.2 million
• Remaining 2026 and 2027 sensor hosting and fabrication commitments: more than US$10 million

What to watch: cash balance and sensor construction additions in the fourth-quarter report. After paying Spire and merger bills, NorthStar must collect its C$13.8 million in customer receivables on time to pay sensor vendors without raising more money.

🔴🔴 𝐎𝐧𝐞 𝐂𝐮𝐬𝐭𝐨𝐦𝐞𝐫 𝐒𝐮𝐩𝐩𝐥𝐢𝐞𝐝 𝐍𝐞𝐚𝐫𝐥𝐲 𝐀𝐥𝐥 𝐓𝐡𝐢𝐫𝐝-𝐐𝐮𝐚𝐫𝐭𝐞𝐫 𝐒𝐚𝐥𝐞𝐬
NorthStar sells space tracking services to defense and civil agencies in Canada, the United States and Europe, and aims to broaden its customer base. In the third quarter, however, its contract with Canada's 3 CSD generated C$16.8 million, or 98% of total revenue. Meanwhile, older contracts wound down by C$1.2 million, and C$7.8 million of the quarter's sales came from "an expanded service offering and services and data previously provided".

Outside Canada, sales shrank. United States service revenue dropped 94.8% from a year ago to C$65,000, while European Union service revenue rose 44.8% to C$291,000. Relying on one defense department for 98% of revenue — and on one-off catch-up billing for nearly half of the quarter's total — leaves the business exposed if Canadian defense priorities shift or if new US and European orders do not replace completed milestone work.

What to watch: revenue from customers outside Canada in the fourth quarter. A rebound in US and European sales is needed to show that NorthStar's eight active government contracts can reduce its reliance on a single buyer.

🔴 𝐁𝐚𝐜𝐤𝐥𝐨𝐠 𝐂𝐨𝐯𝐞𝐫𝐬 𝐔𝐧𝐝𝐞𝐫 𝐇𝐚𝐥𝐟 𝐨𝐟 𝐅𝐨𝐮𝐫𝐭𝐡-𝐐𝐮𝐚𝐫𝐭𝐞𝐫 𝐏𝐥𝐚𝐧
Management tracks backlog — contracted work not yet recognized as revenue, excluding unexercised options — to measure booked future sales. Backlog rose 31.6% from June to C$10.4 million at September 30, which means the space data group added C$19.7 million in new awards and contract modifications during the third quarter by our math.

Even so, NorthStar expects to recognize only 65.4% of that backlog, or about C$6.8 million, in the fourth quarter. Reaching the reiterated C$41 million full-year revenue target requires C$15.1 million to C$15.4 million in fourth-quarter sales by our math, leaving more than C$8 million that was not in backlog at quarter-end. Management noted that hitting its full-year target depends on "securing anticipated new contract awards and modifications on the expected timing".

What to watch: fourth-quarter revenue against the implied C$15.1 million target. Hitting the number would prove NorthStar can sign and deliver fast-turn government modifications within a single quarter.

👓 𝐎𝐭𝐡𝐞𝐫 𝐓𝐡𝐞𝐦𝐞𝐬

𝐌𝐞𝐫𝐠𝐞𝐫 𝐒𝐰𝐚𝐩𝐬 𝐃𝐞𝐛𝐭 𝐅𝐨𝐫 𝐒𝐡𝐚𝐫𝐞 𝐄𝐚𝐫𝐧𝐨𝐮𝐭 𝐋𝐢𝐚𝐛𝐢𝐥𝐢𝐭𝐢𝐞𝐬
Closing the merger with Viking on October 1 reshaped the balance sheet. NorthStar converted C$110.7 million of convertible debentures and C$5.6 million of shareholder loans into common stock, and paid off a EUR 1.3 million note to Thales Alenia Space. In their place, it recorded a C$109.0 million liability for up to 10 million earnout shares, which settles in stock if revenue targets are met but will cause quarterly non-cash profit swings.

— • — • —

𝐀𝐜𝐜𝐨𝐮𝐧𝐭𝐬 𝐫𝐞𝐜𝐞𝐢𝐯𝐚𝐛𝐥𝐞 (𝟐𝟔𝐐𝟑): 𝐂$𝟏𝟑.𝟖 𝐦𝐢𝐥𝐥𝐢𝐨𝐧  ⇗ accelerating

The Governor called on voters to support the APC governorship candidate, Ahmed Galadima Aminu, expressing confidence that he would deliver fairness and good governance across all parts of the state. Galadima also promised to build on the developmental achievements of Governor Fintiri.

text:
The Zos Kia Cultus Crowd...

Austin Osman Spare
and the
Zos Kia Cultus
from LuckyMojo Website

H.P. Lovecraft, in one of his tales of terror, alludes to certain entities which have their being "not in the spaces known to us, but between them. They walk calm and primal, of no dimensions, and to us unseen."

This aptly describes Austin Osman Spare. The circumstances of his birth emphasize the element of ambivalence and inbetweeness which forms the theme of his magic. He told me he was not sure whether he was born on the last day of December 1888, or on New Year's Day, 1889; whether, as he put it, he was Janus backward-turning, or Janus forward-facing. But whichever aspect of the deity he more closely represented, it is a fact that his life was a curious blend of past and future. Despite his inability to remember quite when he was born, the place was certainly Snowhill, London: he was the only son of a City of London policeman.

When barely twenty years of age he began writing The Book of Pleasure, in which he used art and sex to explore the subconscious mind. The Book of Pleasure reeks of diabolism to such an extent that Mario Praz in The Romantic Agony (Oxford, 1933) refers to Spare as an English "satanic occultist", and he places him in the same category as Aleister Crowley.

Spare's intense interest in the more obscure aspects of sorcery sprang from his early friendship with an old colonial woman who claimed descent from a line of Salem witches that Cotton Mather had failed to exterminate. Spare always alluded to her as Mrs. Paterson, and called her his "second mother". She had an extremely limited vocabulary composed mainly of the fortune-teller's argot, yet she was able to define and explain the most abstract ideas much more clearly than could Spare with his large and unusual vocabulary.

Although penniless, she would accept no payment for her fortune-telling, but insisted on the odd symbolic coin traditionally exacted as a sacrifice fee. Apart from her skill in divining, she was the only person Spare ever met who could materialize thoughts to visible appearance. Aleister Crowley- who met and attracted all kinds of psychically active individuals-met two only in the course of his life who had this particular siddhi (Allan Bennett was one; the other, Crowley did not name).

Mrs. Paterson, when visited for purposes of fortune-telling, would read a person's character immediately as a matter of course before going into details about the future. If she prophesied an event she was unable to describe verbally, she would objectivize the event in a visual image and the querent would see, in some dark corner of her room, a clearly defined if fleeting image of the prophesied event. And this never failed to follow at the appointed time.

It was undoubtedly Mrs. Paterson's influence that stimulated Spare's innate interest in the occult, which, allied to his remarkable skill as a draughtsman enabled him to reproduce through his art the strange entities he encountered in transmundane spheres. He drew several portraits of Mrs. Paterson, one of which appeared in The Focus of Life, published by the Morland Press in 1921. Another drawing of her by Spare recently appeared (1971) in the part-work encyclopaedia Man, Myth and Magic, where she is shown after having "exteriorized" herself in the form of a nubile girl.

Spare too was able occasionally to conjure thought-forms to visible appearance, but whereas in the old witch's case it was an unfailing power, in his own case it was erratic and uncertain. On one occasion it worked only too effectively, as two unfortunate persons learnt to their cost. They were of the dilettante kind, mere dabblers in the occult. They wanted Spare to conjure an Elemental to visible appearance. They had seen materialized spirits of the dead in the seance room, but had never seen an Elemental. Spare tried to dissuade them, explaining that such creatures were subconscious automata inhabiting the human psyche at levels normally inaccessible to the conscious mind. As they almost always embodied atavistic urges and propensities, it was an act of folly to evoke them as their intrusion into waking life could be extremely dangerous. But the smatterers did not take him seriously.

Using his own method of elemental evocation, Spare set to work. Nothing happened for some time, then a greenish vapour, resembling fluid seaweed, gradually invaded the room. Tenuous fingers of mist began to congeal into a definite, organized shape. It entered their midst, gaining more solidity with each successive moment. The atmosphere grew miasmic with its presence and an overpowering stench accompanied it; and in the massive cloud of horror that enveloped them, two pinpoints of fire glowed like eyes, blinking in an idiot face which suddenly seemed to fill all space. As it grew in size the couple panicked and implored Spare to drive the thing away. He banished it accordingly. It seemed to crinkle and diminish, then it fell apart like a blanket swiftly disintegrating. But while it had cohered and hung in the room like a cloud, it was virtually opaque and tangible; and it reeked of evil. Both the people concerned were fundamentally changed. Within weeks, one died of no apparent cause; the other had to be committed to an insane asylum.

Although Spare was convinced that an occult Intelligence frequently painted, drew, or wrote through him, he was unable to discover its identity. He was, however, in almost daily contact with a familiar, a spirit-guide, known as Black Eagle whom he had clearly seen and drawn on several occasions. But he was convinced that Black Eagle was not the sole source of his automatism. Spare had but to turn his head suddenly and he would sometimes catch a glimpse of the familiar spirits that constantly surrounded him. Several times he had "caught" one of them long enough to make a lightning-swift sketch.

Spare's frequent traffic with denizens of invisible realms led to his evolving a graphic means of conjoining all thoughts- past, present, and future- in the ever-fluid ether of Consciousness. His graphic symbology represents a definite language designed to facilitate communication with the psychic and subliminal world.

It was Spare's opinion that for this language to be truly effective, each individual should evolve his own, creating his sigils from the material nearest to hand- his own subconscious. He gave as a reason for so much failure in divination the fact that, although the operator sometimes succeeded in annexing traditional symbols to his own subconscious awareness of their true values, many of the symbols eluded correct interpretation; they therefore failed of nexus and were consequently sterile.

Not only could Spare "tell fortunes" in the usually accepted sense, he could also use the cards for influencing the host of subtle entities which swarm in the astral light, and with their cooperation he accomplished much of his magic.

He designed and used a pack of cards which he called the "Arena of Anon", each card bearing a magical emblem which was a variation of one of the letters of the Alphabet of Desire. (The basis of this Alphabet, together with many early examples of the letters composing it, is given in Spare's 'The Book of Pleasure', on which he began working in 1909 and published privately on completion, in 1913.) When vividly visualized, the emblem or sigil mysteriously stirs the subconscious and a corresponding image, or set of images, arises in the mind. In proportion to the power of belief in the sigil, so is the clarity of the image which it evokes. If the sigil taps a layer of ancient or cosmic memory, some astonishing images surge into the mind and the skilful sorcerer is able to project them into the astral mind-stuff of other individuals, so that they imagine the image to be a palpable presence.

Spare could influence elemental phenomena as well as the minds of other people. Great danger lies in possession, and Spare wisely refrained from writing too openly about the processes he employed. What I know about his methods I learnt from personal contact with him.

Even as a child, Spare employed these curious sigils. One is reminded of Yeat's words in The Trembling of the Veil:

"Mathers described how as a boy he had drawn over and over again some event that he longed for; and called those drawings an instinctive magic."

When he was seventeen Spare stayed at the home of the Rev. Robert Hugh Benson, author of The Necromancers and other occult novels. They went out for a walk one summer day; a serene and cloudless blue sky shone overhead. It had been fine all day, and Benson was curious to know whether Spare could, in such unlikely circumstances, produce rain by magical means. Spare said he could, proceeded to trace a sigil on the back of a used envelope, and, pausing in his tracks, concentrated all his attention upon it. Within ten minutes small clouds began to appear; they massed at a point immediately above their heads and discharged violently. Both Benson and Spare were drenched to the skin.

A year or two later, Benson introduced Spare to the Hon. Everard Feilding, Secretary of the Society of Psychic Research. At the time Feilding was associated with Frederick Bligh Bond, the President of the Archaeological Society who, by psychic means, had discovered the buried Edgar Chapel at Glastonbury Abbey. Like Benson, Feilding wanted proof of Spare's magical powers and, when the latter offered to oblige, proposed the following test: Spare was to materialize an object which Feilding mentally visualized without giving any clue as to its nature.

Spare drew one of his magical sigils, which, instead of being symbolic of the unknown desired object, was the ideograph of a familiar spirit whose services he frequently employed when any mind-reading was required.

After some time, Spare received a vivid impression of the object in Feilding's mind. He then drew a second sigil, told Feilding he need no longer concentrate, and proceeded to do so himself. These proceedings were interrupted by a knock on the door. Feilding tiptoed to the door, opened it, and was amazed to find his valet proffering a pair of slippers. Feilding turned to Spare and asked him how he had done it!

An essential part of Spare's technique lay in deliberate forgetfulness, and this is the part which a novice finds extremely difficult. One is reminded of the king who lavished a fortune on an itinerant alchemist who had successfully manufactured the Philosopher's Stone. After giving the king lengthy and complicated instructions, which the king repeated by heart, the alchemist smiled and said approvingly:

"Yes, your Highness has remembered every detail perfectly; there is just one further point to remember. For three minutes before the Alchemical Substance congeals, you must concentrate your mind upon its lustre as it seethes in the alembic, but during this time you should on no account let the thought of greenness cross you mind for even a moment."

The king thanked the alchemist and prepared to make the Stone. Everything went according to plan until the last few minutes, when the mind of the king was invaded by an army of green objects which he was powerless to banish.

With Spare's sigils the case is somewhat similar. The reason he gives for forgetting the desire at the time of invoking it lies in the fact that for the operation to succeed the conscious mind must have no inkling of the transaction. Consciously formulated desires take time to materialize; subconscious desires can be made to materialize very swiftly. Consciousness of the desire vitiates the entire process, so a method had to be found of forgetting the desire during the period of magical evocation. Spare called the process "union through absent-mindedness" and advocated the yogic method of emptying the mind of all but the sigil. This is not always successful so as an alternative he suggests the sigillization of perennial desires, desires that are sure to arise periodically, as for instance the desire for beautiful women. Several such desires are then sigillized, scrambled together, and laid aside for several days. On reassembling the cards upon which they have been drawn, the operator is unable to remember precisely what sigillizes what! The rite is then comparatively easy to accomplish for it requires only concentrated thought.

Spare often supplemented the process by a sexual formula which endowed it with added efficacy. He derived most of his sex-magical formulae from a Delphic Pythoness who communed with him during sessions of automatic writing. This Delphic Oracle was probably the spirit of old Mrs. Paterson, guiding him from beyond.

One such formula enabled him to "give life to the autistic, by an earthenware virgin". In view of the present-day predilection for auto-erotic aids to ecstasy, the resuscitation of the dildo (At the time of writing, my attention has been drawn to "the first European sex paper" which reflects the current obsession with purely mechanistic aspects of self-love. Nevertheless, such methods employed in a magical manner may place the practitioner in direct contact with his daemon or genius.) and the widespread curiosity about the sorcery of sex, Spare's formula of the Earthenware Virgin is of particular interest, though for Spare it had an exclusively magical aim.

Until he received this formula he had, as he put it, "copulated merely with the atmosphere, or rode whores, witches and bitches of all kinds, there being few virgins".

In order to translate a specified desire from the level of subjective consciousness to the material or objective plane, the Pythoness instructed him to construct an urn in conformity with the dimensions of the erect penis. Sufficient space- but no more- was to be left at the end of the vessel in order to form a vacuum when the phallus was inserted. The cavity was to contain the sigillized wish, which was automatically consecrated at the moment of orgasm. The greatly enhanced pleasure induced by the suctional power of the vacuum increased the size of the penis and caused an unusually prolonged orgasm. At the critical moment, the desire was to be vividly visualized and held steadily in mind for as long as possible. When the mental image began to wane and disappear the urn was hermetically sealed and buried in a casket filled with earth, or in the ground itself.

Spare maintained that this was the formula used by the ancient Greek urnings; hence the designation. In one of his unpublished writings he give the following instructions:

"Bury the urn at midnight, the moon being quartered. When the moon wanes, disinter the urn and- while repeating a suitable incantation- pour its contents as a libation on to the earth. Then re-bury it."

As the sperm would by that time have congealed, Spare advised a replenishment before the second "burial". He describes the Earthenware Virgin as "the most formidable formula known; it never fails and is dangerous. Hence, what is not written down must be guessed.

"From this formula was derived the legend of the genii of the brazen vessel associated with Solomon."

Whether this is so, I do not know, but there is a curious illustration in Payne Knight's celebrated Discourse on the Worship of Priapus (London, 1865) which is not satisfactorily explained in the text. It is in two parts and depicts a male figure with sexual organ erect; in his raised right hand he holds a vase-shaped sheath which he is about to clamp upon the phallus. The second part of the illustration shows the same image, but with penis drooping languidly after ejaculation, and the waist of the figure girdled with fruits symbolic of the rite's fulfilment. There are also one or two illustrations in Reinach's Repertoire des Vases Peints (Paris, 1899), which suggest a similar magical practice.

Spare could undoubtedly materialize atavisms from his own subconsciousness and clothe them fleetingly in the sexual ectoplasm (or astral semen) of his atmospheric copulations.

Occasionally, these entities actually achieved a degree of density sufficient to make them visible- and even palpable- to other people. He called them "elemental automata" or "intrusive familiars". They frequently copulated amongst themselves, engendering offspring simultaneously. Spare has depicted many of these creatures in their peculiar pursuits and has written several accounts of the Sabbath which he attended in their company. Old Mrs. Paterson's influence is here very marked, for he used her likeness as the type of the ancient witch in many of his drawings.

One of Spare's constantly recurring themes concerns the transmogrification of age into youth. The first time Mrs. Paterson transformed herself before his eyes, the sorcery of it left a permanent impression which inspired many of his later works. One moment she was the lined and wizened old crone, then, in a flash, she appeared to him as a syren equipped with all the allurements of sex-appeal, an image that fulfilled his penchant for full voluptuous contours. How she projected such a glamour he was unable to discover, and although he never surprised her secret, he tried- with paartial success- to emulate her example. This he did by a magical induction of ecstasy which enabled him to function at levels of high emotionalism. He was at such times creatively active for days on end, needing neither food nor sleep. Enhanced sexual activity accompanied this condition. On the few occasions when he did not sublimate this energy and direct it to artistic creation, he regretted it. Such was his hunger that in one night alone he coupled with eighteen women. He called these outbursts j"Dionysiac spasms of pan-sexualism", in which he had a vision of "all things fornicating all the time".

Spare wrote down his witch-guide's instructions and, over the years, worked them into several books which he illustrated by some of the best of his drawings. It was only towards the end of his life, however, that he concentrated the mass of Mrs. Paterson's teachings into definite form. This consisted of a series of aphorisms and a magical grimoire which he was working on at the time of his death in 1956. Both these works survive in manuscript. He intended calling the Grimoire The Book of the Living Word of Zos, the name Zos being his magical name in the Witch-Cult.

The Grimoire is not so much a resume of the Witch Tradition as a highly individualized system of sorcery reflecting his creative genius and aesthetic theories. He also developed and extended his magical alphabet, the Atavistic Alphabet about which he had first written in The Book of Pleasure in 1913. Each letter represents a sex-principle potent to awaken remote atavistic strata of the psyche. Examples of its use are given in the Grimoire, where he allies it with Witchcraft. The following is a literal translation of one of his favourite spells:

O mighty Rehctaw! Thou who exists in all erogenousness, We evoke Thee!
By the power of the meanings arising from these forms I make. We evoke Thee!
By the Talismans that speak the secret leitmotif of desire, We evoke Thee!
By the sacrifices, abstinences and transvaluations we make, We evoke Thee!
By the sacred inbetweeness concepts Give us the flesh!
By the quadriga sexualis Give us unvarying desire!
By the conquest of fatigue Give us eternal resurgence!
By the most sacred Word-graph of Heaven We invoke Thee!

This prayer or evocation embodies traditional Sabbatic concepts and might be described as the Alpha and Omega of Spare's doctrine.
Rehctaw (Watcher) is spelt backwards, not for the reason given in connection with Dee and Kelly's angelic communications but because the "backward" symbolism conceals the key to the reification of desire, the final absorption of the ego-current in its source- the Self. Hence Spare's emphasis on Self-love, or autotelic ecstasy. Rehctaw is the symbol of reaching backwards in time to infinite remoteness by the mechanism of intense nostalgia. Whether it is symbolized by the Moon presiding over the nocturnal orgies of the Sabbath, or by the back-to-back dance of the witches and warlocks (see de L'Ancre), or by the infamous kiss of the Sabbath which is applied to the anus of the Demon; all such symbols indicate an infinite regression which causes atavistic resurgence and the inversion of sex to Self-love.
"Shall I speak of that unique intensity without form? Know ye the ecstasy within? The pleasure between ego and self? At that time of ecstasy there is no thought of others; there is no thought." (The Anathema of Zos, by A.O. Spare; London, 1927)
The opening line of the evocation resumes the method employed at the Sabbath for conscious wish-fulfilment through self-pleasure, and it is glossed by the words:
"Except in the sensuous impact of flesh on flesh there are no meanings."
The Self lives in, permeates, and is identical with, Reality- the enduring and ever present Consciousness- the living flesh compact of endlessly reifying dream.
The second part of the evocation refers to the sigils and letters of the sacred alphabet wherewith Zos (i.e. the body considered as a whole) produces its subtle spells by projecting its Self on the mists of matter, without. In other words, the language of desire and its meanings penetrate the silent regions of consciously forgotten experiences, evoking by its rebverberant power the ineluctable memories that abide perpetually in subconsciousness.
"The Talismans that speak the leitmotif of desire" are, primarily, the two major magical instruments of Spare's system- the Hand and Eye of which the phallus and the kteis are the secret symbols. They are both used, as in Crowley's Cult, for evoking or provoking "consciousness in touch; ecstasy in vision".
The fourth clause of the Sabbatic Prayer refers to the occult maxim that great achievements proceed upon total exhaustion of energy in one great burst of release, after a period- long or short- of sacrifice or abstention, during which time the necessary energy is accumulated and intensified. "The Sabbath is always secret, communal and periodic; an enforced consummation for almost unlimited wish-fulfilment."

"Prolonged voluntary abstinence, repression and sacrifice, is released in mass sexual congress and sublimated to one end: the exteriorization of a wish, which is thus achieved by a great saving and a total spending." (From an unpublished manuscript, Formula of the Witch's Sabbath as first told me by a Witch, by A.O.S.)

The "transvaluations" are effected by the sloughing of conventional ideas and beliefs, and by the absorption of the energy thus liberated. Spare terms such energy "free belief". It is this aimless energy that is seized upon at the Sabbath and directed to given ends.

The fifth clause of the Prayer introduces one of the most important aspects of Spare's magic, that of inbetweenness.

In everyday life one craze or "belief" follows another. By a process of not-believing, of emptying the craze, or obsession, of its content, we can surprise the tendency of belief to appear as one thing rather than another, or as one thing after another. We can in this way break through into that ecstasy of communion with the Atmospheric "I" which Spare calls the Kia, the state of inbetweenness, or Neither-Neither.

The primordial belief is "Self", "God", or Kia (it does not matter what we call it). It is the only belief that is self-evident because it is experienced by each one of us at every moment of our existence. It is also the only belief that is truly free of belief, because to be is to be-live it- as Spare aptly expresses it. It is void of necessity to become anything else, for it is all things all the time and can only and always be itself. If we can realize this we shall not fall into the error of conceptual thought, which constantly breeds other thoughts with which we temporarily identify ourselves: the Buddhist cycle of birth, death and rebirth.

In a few words, Spare states the crux of the doctrine: "By hindering belief and semen from conception, they become simple and cosmic." Only when desire has become cosmic can the total ecstasy, which characterizes Kia, dawn in the individual consciousness, because it is then no longer limited or personalized consciousness, but cosmic in scope and free to enjoy itself eternally.

In other words, one must enlarge belief or desire until it embraces all things; Spare urges us to will "insatiety of desire, brave self-indulgence and primaeval sexualism" (The Focus of Life, by Austin O. Spare. The Morland Press, London, 1921.), for belief freed from conception merges desire with the Infinite, creates a unity of Self-Knowing (which is also supreme Self-Love) and transcends the two poles of objectivity and subjectivity, discovering in between the two, the Real Self, Kia, the Atmospheric "I".

2K AND ZYNGA: DIVERSIFICATION DOESN'T ELIMINATE EARNINGS VOLATILITY
For FY2027, Take-Two expects its major publishing labels to contribute approximately 37% of Net Bookings from Rockstar Games, 34% from Zynga, and 29% from 2K. These percentages describe expected sales mix, not precise profit contributions or an allocation of GTA VI's value across the group. Even in the year of its biggest launch, Take-Two's other businesses still account for the majority of activity.

NBA 2K27 launched on September 4 and, according to management, surpassed 4 million units sold by November. Over a comparable period, the game delivered the second-highest Net Bookings performance in franchise history. Even so, it fell short of Take-Two's internal plan. That is an important lesson for investors. A popular product can still be a financial disappointment if management had penciled in even stronger growth, higher player spending, or a level of profitability that the actual results fail to deliver. Management pointed to intense competition for players' attention and outlined plans for new seasons and additional content. The question is whether those initiatives translate into higher Net Bookings, not merely more headlines and social media engagement.

2K also operates franchises including Borderlands, Mafia, Civilization, WWE 2K, and PGA TOUR 2K. A broad catalog reduces dependence on any one title, but it does not ensure that every release earns an attractive return. During 2026, some games received updates and additional content, while other projects were delayed or scaled back. Work on Borderlands 4 for Switch 2 was suspended, and the NFL 2K initiative did not proceed in its originally planned form. Portfolio breadth alone does not eliminate execution risk.

Zynga operates under a different business model, with greater exposure to mobile gaming, advertising, and ongoing player activity. In Q2 FY2027, mobile Net Bookings fell from $818.1 million to $707.6 million, a 13.5% decline. Color Block Jam weakened against an exceptionally strong year-earlier comparison, while Match Factory! also underperformed. At the same time, Toon Blast grew Net Bookings by 4%, Words With Friends increased 6%, and Top Goal remained in limited rollout. The company also reported quarter-over-quarter growth in its advertising business.

In China, NBA 2K All-Star, developed in partnership with Tencent, surpassed 11 million registered users, according to management. Take-Two described the game's margins as attractive. However, registered users are not the same as paying customers. Without detailed financial disclosures, there is no reliable way to calculate the game's contribution to consolidated earnings.

Another opportunity for Zynga is direct-to-consumer (DTC) distribution. By reducing reliance on intermediaries, publishers may retain a larger share of player spending and gain greater control over their customer relationships. The channel is expanding, but Take-Two has not disclosed enough data to quantify its future impact on group-level margins.

Overall, I view the diversification story as moderately positive. Rockstar, 2K, and Zynga serve different audiences and monetize their products in different ways, allowing established franchises to support the company between major launches. But NBA 2K27's shortfall and weakness in parts of the mobile portfolio show that these businesses are not a complete hedge against the risks now concentrated around GTA VI.

CASH FLOW: THE REAL TEST GOES BEYOND RECORD SALES
The most convincing financial evidence of GTA VI's success will not be the preorder count. It will be the cash Take-Two actually gets to keep. For now, the cash flow picture has deteriorated. During the first six months of FY2027, operating cash flow came in at negative $173.5 million, compared with positive $83.7 million a year earlier. That represents a $257.2 million deterioration. Capital expenditures increased from $57.0 million to $163.3 million. As a result, simplified free cash flow-operating cash flow less capital expenditures-fell from positive $26.7 million to negative $336.8 million.

That does not, by itself, signal a financial crisis. Ahead of a major launch, cash can leave the business long before the anticipated sales start flowing in. The cash flow statement includes $372.4 million in outflows related to software development and licensing. Importantly, that amount is already reflected in operating cash flow. Subtracting it again when calculating FCF would double-count the expense. Inventories, prepaid expenses, and other assets also increased, while deferred revenue declined. Take-Two has been funding preparations for future sales. Whether those investments pay off depends on its ability to deliver against the plan.

One notable expenditure involved the August acquisition of a London property that the company had previously leased. The capitalized value of the asset was approximately $91.8 million. That full accounting value should not be treated as an equivalent one-time cash payment, since the transaction also involved the settlement of the existing lease arrangement.

As of November, management continued to expect more than $1 billion in operating cash flow for FY2027. After posting negative $173.5 million in the first half, Take-Two would need to generate more than $1.1735 billion in positive operating cash flow during the second half to reach that target. With full-year capital expenditures projected at approximately $290 million, simplified FCF would exceed roughly $710 million if management delivers on its cash flow outlook. That is a forward-looking scenario, not a realized result.

If GTA VI produces enormous Net Bookings but weak cash conversion, the financial payoff will be less impressive than the headline sales figures suggest. Ultimately, the economics of this release cycle will be validated by the combination of sales, profitability, cash generation, and the company's ability to reduce debt.

$2.5773 BILLION IN CAPITALIZED COSTS IS NOT GTA VI'S DEVELOPMENT BUDGET
As of September 30, Take-Two reported $2.4949 billion in long-term capitalized software development and licensing costs, along with $82.4 million classified as current. Combined, those assets totaled approximately $2.5773 billion, representing 27.5% of the group's total assets. The long-term portion alone had increased by approximately $217.4 million since March.

This accounting treatment cuts both ways. Development spending incurred today can be capitalized and recognized as an expense later, when the underlying games begin generating revenue. That helps match production costs with the periods in which the products are monetized. But capitalization does not eliminate the risk that some investments will fail to generate adequate returns. The write-down of a canceled game in the first quarter is a clear example.

Crucially, the $2.5773 billion balance covers multiple projects across the entire Take-Two group. It is not a disclosed development budget for GTA VI. Nor should we assume that the entire amount will begin amortizing in November. The timing and pace of expense recognition depend on the individual titles and their release schedules. A credible assessment of GTA VI's standalone profit margin would require information about its full development budget, marketing costs, amortization, revenue, and ongoing operating expenses. Take-Two has not disclosed those figures. Ignoring these costs would distort the analysis. Attributing the entire capitalized balance to GTA VI would be equally misleading.

THE BALANCE SHEET PROVIDES A CUSHION, BUT DEBT MATURITIES STILL MATTER
At the end of September, Take-Two held $1.1494 billion in cash and cash equivalents, plus $524.2 million in short-term investments. That represents approximately $1.6736 billion in available cash and investments, excluding restricted cash. Financial debt, measured at its carrying value, totaled approximately $2.5198 billion. Subtracting cash and short-term investments produces simplified net debt of approximately $846.2 million, compared with roughly $528.7 million in March. Net debt therefore increased by approximately $317.5 million. That increase primarily reflects a reduction in the company's cash cushion, rather than a comparable increase in gross borrowings.

Take-Two also had approximately $997.9 million available under an undrawn revolving credit facility. That provides an additional liquidity backstop, but it is not cash already sitting on the balance sheet. Drawing on the facility would create additional borrowing obligations under the applicable terms.

The debt maturity schedule deserves attention. Approximately $29.4 million in remaining convertible notes comes due on December 15, 2026. Another $600 million in notes matures on April 14, 2027, followed by $800 million in March 2028. Take-Two has previously repaid debt using, among other sources, proceeds from equity issuance. Short-term debt increased to $629.2 million at the end of September, largely because approaching maturities were reclassified from long-term liabilities. That should not be mistaken for the company taking out an entirely new loan of the same amount.

I do not see evidence of an immediate solvency threat in these figures. The company has cash, short-term investments, and access to additional credit. Management has also indicated that GTA VI-related cash inflows could allow Take-Two to finish FY2027 in a net cash position. But that remains to be demonstrated. Between management's projections and the March year-end balance sheet lies a major test: can the launch fund ongoing operations, future development, and scheduled debt repayments without a meaningful increase in borrowing or shareholder dilution?

PLATFORM OWNERS CONTROL THE ROAD TO THE CUSTOMER
Owning one of the world's most valuable gaming franchises does not make Take-Two independent of distribution platforms. In FY2026, the company's five largest customers accounted for a combined 80.6% of GAAP revenue. Take-Two disclosed that Apple, Sony, Google, and Microsoft each individually represented more than 10%. During the first half of FY2027, revenue concentration among the five largest customers increased to 80.8%. Four customers individually accounted for 27.1%, 20.7%, 14.7%, and 11.9% of group revenue. However, the quarterly filing did not identify which company corresponded to each percentage. Assigning those figures to specific platform operators would therefore be speculation.

Console manufacturers and mobile storefront operators control player access, distribution rules, product approvals, and financial settlements. A franchise as powerful as GTA gives Take-Two considerable negotiating leverage. It does not eliminate platform dependence.

One agreement that merits particular attention is Take-Two's global publishing arrangement with Sony. According to the FY2026 annual report, the current contractual term expires on March 31, 2027, with provisions for automatic annual renewals. Sony nevertheless retains the right to terminate the agreement with or without cause upon 30 days' notice. That does not mean termination is likely. The commercial incentives for both parties strongly favor maintaining the relationship. But the contractual language highlights a meaningful asymmetry in their respective rights.

Take-Two also entered into a new long-term agreement with Microsoft, signed on September 28, 2026, and effective September 17. The agreement replaces earlier Xbox-related arrangements and governs areas including publishing, physical and digital distribution, compensation, and product approvals. Some of the economic terms remain confidential. As a result, the agreement cannot be used to infer specific GTA VI margins or guaranteed payments. It provides a more predictable framework for cooperation, not a publicly disclosed sales contract with a known dollar value.

Xbox Cloud Gaming and Zynga's direct-to-consumer initiatives address a similar strategic question from different angles: Who owns the customer relationship, and who captures the economics of the money players spend? Both initiatives offer potential upside. Neither provides enough disclosed financial data to attach a reliable dollar value to that upside.

SHAREHOLDERS OWN A CLAIM ON THE BUSINESS, NOT JUST ITS REVENUE
Take-Two does not pay a regular dividend. It also conducted no share repurchases during the September quarter, despite having an authorized buyback program. Shareholder returns therefore depend primarily on the company's future earnings power and the valuation investors are willing to assign to it.

The share count matters as well. At the end of March 2026, Take-Two had approximately 185.4 million shares outstanding. By October 26, that figure had risen to 187,213,488 shares-an increase of roughly 1% in just a few months. Stock-based compensation expense reached $176.0 million in the first half of FY2027, compared with $136.6 million a year earlier. Management expects approximately $462 million in stock-based compensation for the full fiscal year. Those accounting costs cannot be translated directly into an equivalent percentage of dilution. The terms and settlement methods of individual awards matter. But the underlying risk is clear. Even if the company's total equity value increases, the benefit per share can be diluted if the ownership base keeps expanding.

In June, Take-Two disclosed the potential settlement of up to 329,949 shares associated with incentive units granted to ZMC Advisors, a management-affiliated entity. If fully settled, that maximum issuance would represent approximately 0.18% of the resulting share count. This was not an equity offering to public investors in exchange for fresh cash. Related-party filings also show sales of certain shares, including transactions intended to cover tax obligations. Without distinguishing tax-related sales and other administrative transactions from genuine changes in insiders' investment convictions, I would not interpret insider selling alone as evidence that management lacks confidence in GTA VI.

In September, shareholders also approved a charter amendment limiting the liability of certain corporate officers to the extent permitted under Delaware law. That is a corporate governance issue. The available information does not support assigning a specific numerical valuation impact to the change.

RISKS THAT DON'T SHOW UP DIRECTLY ON THE INCOME STATEMENT
In April, Rockstar confirmed a limited data-related incident involving the systems of an external service provider. According to the company, the incident did not affect operations or players. There is no sound basis for estimating a financial loss or attributing an impact on GTA VI's launch. Nevertheless, the episode highlights exposure to third-party vendors and cybersecurity risks.

A separate labor dispute has been unfolding in the United Kingdom. Former Rockstar employees and union representatives have linked certain dismissals to union activity. The company has rejected those allegations, citing confidentiality violations. A vote concerning formal union recognition within Rockstar's U.K. operations began on November 12 and was scheduled to run through November 26. As of the information cutoff for this analysis, neither the dispute nor the vote had reached a final resolution. The situation could affect workforce management, reputation, and operating costs.

Artificial intelligence presents another longer-term variable. Google's January demonstration of its Project Genie prototype drew market attention to the possibility of generating interactive worlds using AI. That demonstration, however, does not establish that current AI tools can replace the sophisticated design, production, marketing, and long-term support required for a GTA-scale game. Over time, AI could both lower certain development costs and intensify competition, potentially reshaping the competitive advantages of major publishers. The direction and magnitude of its eventual financial impact on Take-Two cannot yet be estimated with confidence.

STOCK PERFORMANCE AND VALUATION: A MUCH BETTER FUTURE IS ALREADY PRICED IN
Take-Two shares closed at $256.03 on December 31, 2025. By November 11, 2026, the stock was trading at $231.31, representing a decline of approximately 9.66%. Over the same period, the price-only S&P 500 index increased from 6,845.50 to 7,619.38, a gain of 11.30%. That puts TTWO's relative underperformance at approximately 20.96 percentage points. The comparison excludes index dividends, so it should not be interpreted as a total-return comparison.

More recently, the stock staged a sharp rebound. TTWO closed at $207.40 on November 9, surged to $224.64 on November 10 (+8.31%), and climbed again to $231.31 on November 11 (+2.97%). Across those final two trading sessions, shares gained approximately 11.53% relative to the November 9 close. The rally coincided with management reaffirming guidance, the earnings release, and additional evidence of GTA VI's extraordinary preorder demand.

At $231.31 per share, using the latest confirmed share count of 187,213,488, Take-Two's equity market capitalization is approximately $43.30 billion. Adding simplified net debt of $846.2 million produces an estimated enterprise value (EV) of approximately $44.15 billion. That calculation combines the November 11 share price, the October 26 share count, and the September 30 balance sheet. It does not fully incorporate lease obligations or other adjustments sometimes included in more comprehensive enterprise value calculations.

Against FY2027 guidance, the resulting EV represents approximately 5.38-5.52x Net Bookings and 5.40-5.53x GAAP revenue. I would not characterize those multiples as cheap, particularly given the company's weak current profitability. Net Bookings are not earnings. Between a customer's purchase and cash that ultimately accrues to shareholders lie development costs, platform fees, amortization, taxes, and additional investment requirements.

The valuation disconnect becomes even more apparent when we compare the stock price with FY2027 GAAP EPS guidance of $0.57–$0.75. At $231.31 per share, TTWO trades at approximately 308–406x projected FY2027 GAAP earnings. That exceptionally high multiple is partly explained by the company's position in its development cycle and amortization associated with historical acquisitions. But it would be difficult to argue that current GAAP earnings, on their own, support the valuation.

Now consider cash flow. If Take-Two delivers more than $1 billion in operating cash flow and spends approximately $290 million on capital expenditures, simplified FY2027 FCF would exceed roughly $710 million. Relative to the company's market capitalization, that implies an FCF yield above approximately 1.64%. That is still a modest near-term cash return relative to the price investors are paying for the business. More importantly, it depends on the company executing a demanding second-half cash flow plan. The market is therefore paying not so much for earnings already reported, but for a substantial expansion in Take-Two's earnings power in FY2028 and beyond.

WALL STREET IS VALUING FY2028, BUT MANAGEMENT HASN'T GUIDED FOR IT YET
November research notes from major banks help explain the optimism embedded in Take-Two's valuation. JPMorgan maintained its Overweight rating and a $310 price target for December 2027. A public summary of its model pointed to approximately $10.59 in adjusted EPS for FY2028. UBS reiterated its Buy rating while lowering its price target from $300 to $295. It also trimmed its FY2028 adjusted EPS estimate from $11.06 to $10.86. Bank of America, having previously reduced its target from $368 to $330, continued to express a positive view and maintained the $330 target following the November results.

These are sell-side analyst forecasts, not commitments made by Take-Two. The material reviewed does not include the banks' complete financial models, so their underlying assumptions cannot be independently reconstructed in full. At $231.31 per share, the FY2028 adjusted EPS forecasts from JPMorgan and UBS imply approximately 21.3-21.8x forward adjusted earnings. That is a striking contrast with the 308–406x multiple implied by FY2027 GAAP EPS. Part of the difference comes from using adjusted rather than GAAP earnings. But the bigger driver is the expectation that profitability will increase dramatically in the following fiscal year. These metrics cannot be directly reconciled without a detailed breakdown of the adjustments.

As of November 12, Take-Two had not yet issued comprehensive official guidance for FY2028. The market may reasonably anticipate that GTA VI will become a multiyear monetization platform. But investors still lack reliable company-level guidance on the actual scale and margins of that future business. If record launch sales are followed by sustained purchases of additional content and a durable player community, today's elevated expectations could ultimately prove justified. If the revenue profile is dominated by a one-time purchasing surge and subsequent periods fall short of expectations, even a record-breaking launch may not be enough to support the current valuation. A bullish analyst rating does not remove that uncertainty.

THE STRONGEST CASE AGAINST BEING TOO BEARISH
It would be easy to look at negative free cash flow, a widening operating loss, and declining first-half Net Bookings, then dismiss the entire growth story. That would be too simplistic. For a publisher preparing one of the biggest launches in gaming history, the six months leading up to release may be a particularly poor period for judging long-term earnings power.

Take-Two has spent years funding a product whose eventual sales could dwarf the company's typical quarterly revenue. Development is complete. Preloading is underway. Sony and Microsoft have independently confirmed unprecedented preorder demand. Management has maintained its financial guidance. And Rockstar has already demonstrated, through GTA V, that it can monetize a successful franchise over an exceptionally long period. Those are meaningful reasons to expect a sharp improvement in financial performance. Take-Two also has deep experience in digital distribution, microtransactions, and managing large, long-lived gaming communities. If demand converts into realized sales and cash receipts, the second half of FY2027 could look radically different from the first.

That is why weak current results do not invalidate the GTA VI bull case. But they do not financially validate it yet, either. A record-breaking product and an attractive investment at a particular share price are not the same thing. What ultimately matters is whether Take-Two's realized cash-generating power exceeds-or falls short of-the expectations already baked into the stock.

WHAT INVESTORS SHOULD WATCH OVER THE COMING MONTHS
The first major catalyst is November 19, 2026. Investors should monitor GTA VI's actual release, availability on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X/S, and technical performance at launch. The following weeks will provide a clearer picture of actual sales, player reception, and how well demand holds up after the initial rush. Official unit sales disclosures would be valuable, although there is no guarantee those figures will be released immediately.

The second major test will come with earnings for the quarter ending December 31, 2026. The key benchmarks are management's guidance of $3.35-$3.50 billion in Net Bookings and $250–$276 million in GAAP net income. Meeting those targets while maintaining healthy profitability would provide strong evidence that Take-Two is successfully converting launch excitement into actual financial performance. Availability issues, weaker-than-expected sales, or poor conversion of orders into recognized revenue would point in the opposite direction.

The third test is cash generation. Management's full-year operating cash flow target of more than $1 billion requires more than $1.1735 billion in positive operating cash flow during the second half. That cash generation needs to be assessed alongside capital spending and changes in debt-not merely Net Bookings.

The fourth test concerns genuine recurring monetization. Some launch-quarter RCS will come from the Ultimate Edition price premium. That means the headline RCS figure alone will tell us little about whether GTA VI is establishing a durable new spending ecosystem. Future disclosures on player engagement, repeat purchases, additional content, new platforms, and any eventual multiplayer offering will be crucial.
